feature: Design study: the last mouse-only controls reach the keyboard
summary: Every clickable thing in the design study now takes focus with Tab and presses with Enter or Space, including the eight page-private controls the shared pass left behind. A page that binds its own click now has one call to make it keyboard-reachable, and the audit fails the build if one is missed.
setup: Dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:8791, open a mock page in the shell. No app build involved.

try.do: Open the design-system modes page and press Tab until the Dark label above the token table lights up.
Press Space. The whole table and the sample switch to Dark, the same as clicking the label.
Open the motion language page and Tab to the Decelerate easing card.
Press Enter. The puck glides across the rail again.
Tab on to the Effects chip in the collapsing-section demo and press Enter to fold it, then Enter again to open it.
Open the image editing page and Tab to the eye on the Hue / Saturation layer.
Press Space. The adjustment switches off on the canvas and the eye closes; Space again brings it back.

evaluate: Is the focus ring on the small eye icon visible enough to find at a glance, or does it need a larger target?
Do the three mode labels above the table earn a tab stop, given the segmented control above them already switches the mode?
When Tab lands on an easing card, is it obvious that Enter will replay it, or does the card need a visible play affordance?
Does the tab order on the image page reach the layer eye in a sensible place, or does it feel buried?
rough: Only the Hue / Saturation eye works; every other eye in the layer list is decoration and is skipped by Tab. That is honest to the mock but a first-time user may try to Tab to the others.
The mode labels are a second path to something the segmented control already does. Kept for keyboard parity, but a redesign could drop them.

An icon is mask-rendered, so a focus ring drawn on the icon itself disappears. The eye became a real button around the icon; any other icon that gains a click should do the same rather than reuse the shortcut helper.
